verdict.rationale: Logseq documents a search bar and a simple-query facility (`{{query Something you're looking for}}`) for asking questions of the knowledge base, and graphs can stay local-only, which implies offline use. The evidence never documents full-text search behavior or explicit filters on tags, properties or paths. A hands-on report says indexing and responsiveness slow down massively on large graphs, which undercuts "instantly". Missing for 10: explicit full-text search documentation, documented tag/property/path filters, evidence that search works offline, evidence of fast search at scale.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can instantly search all my notes with full-text search plus filters on tags, properties, and paths — including offline

citations.quote: Simple queries by using `{{query }}`, the format is something like this: {{query Something you're looking for}}
Queries are for asking questions from your knowledge base
You can also make a new page in the search bar.
Syncing is a choice that is made per graph and thus allows for some graphs to be local only.
